name: A Colorado Springs street

place_source.title: Wikidata: Colorado Springs (Q49258), coordinate location (P625) and elevation above sea level (P2044)

blurb: A dry, high-altitude street block on Colorado's Front Range: honey locust and blue spruce over a scrubby lawn, pinyon and Rocky Mountain juniper on the open ground behind, magpies and scrub-jays in the trees by day, flickers and robins on the grass, squirrels and cottontails at dusk, and raccoons and a great horned owl after dark.

facts.text: Colorado Springs has a cooler, dry-winter monsoon-influenced continental climate (Köppen Dwa/Cwa), with July the warmest month at 21.6 °C.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Colorado Springs", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Colorado Springs", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: At 6,035 feet (1,839 m) the city stands over a mile above sea level, on Fountain Creek 70 miles south of Denver and near the base of Pikes Peak.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Colorado Springs", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Colorado Springs", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The city averages about 16.5 inches (419 mm) of rain a year and 243 sunny days, with most of its summer rainfall arriving in brief afternoon thunderstorms.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Colorado Springs", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Colorado Springs", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Colorado's foothills home deer, fox squirrels, desert cottontails, mountain cottontails and coyote, the wildlife this locale's species list is drawn from.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Colorado", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Colorado", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Woodhouse's scrub-jay, a blue-headed jay of pinyon-juniper woodland, is very common west of the southern Rocky Mountains and will come to feeders in urban areas.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Woodhouse's scrub jay", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Woodhouse's scrub jay", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Great horned owls take up residence in urban areas but prefer park-like settings with less human activity, nesting higher and in larger trees than rural birds.
